chunks.heading: People of the Bark
chunks.notes: Sets up the micro-civilization's scale and states the "quiet moral" framing device directly, with no incident or conflict yet -- pure worldbuilding setup.

chunks.heading: People of the Bark
chunks.notes: The "Tremor" scene opens the narrative on a mundane squirrel misread as cataclysm, then catalogs the bark people's belief system in a bulleted list.

chunks.heading: People of the Bark
chunks.notes: The shadow/hand conflict plays the same their-view-vs-our-view device as the tremor, then the closing "Moral" paragraph shifts into triadic anaphoric repetition to pivot toward affirmation.

chunks.heading: People of the Bark
chunks.notes: A one-line stated aphorism closing the piece, directly asserting that a small life's stakes still carry worth ("Even the smallest world is a universe to the ones who live in it").
